implement.summary:
TERMINATION-FOR-CONVENIENCE CLAUSE — one-year software subscription agreement, law of England and Wales

7. Termination for convenience

In this clause 7: "Fees" means the subscription fees paid by the Customer for the Term (excluding any one-off set-up charges, third-party charges and usage-based charges); "Term" means the one-year term of the subscription (365 days); and "Termination Date" means the date on which this agreement terminates under clause 7.1.

7.1 Either party may terminate this agreement for convenience, at any time and without cause, by giving to the other party not less than thirty (30) days' written notice of termination. This agreement will terminate on the date falling thirty (30) days after that notice is received.

7.2 A notice of termination given under clause 7.1 takes effect on the date on which it is received by the other party (being the date of actual receipt of the notice by the other party or its authorised representative, in accordance with the notices provisions of this agreement), and the thirty (30) day notice period in clause 7.1 runs from that date.

7.3 Where this agreement is terminated under this clause, the Supplier shall refund to the Customer the Fees prepaid by the Customer in respect of the unexpired part of the Term as at the Termination Date, calculated pro rata on a daily basis as the Fees multiplied by the number of whole days in the unexpired part of the Term divided by 365, and paid to the Customer within thirty (30) days after the Termination Date. Such refund is the Customer's sole financial remedy in respect of a termination under this clause, and is without prejudice to any rights or liabilities accrued before the Termination Date or to any provision of this agreement expressed to survive its termination.

MAPPING OF EACH SUB-CLAUSE TO THE THREE TERMS (one line each)

7.1 — carries out term 1: either party may terminate on thirty days' written notice.
7.2 — carries out term 3: a notice takes effect on the date it is received.
7.3 — carries out term 2: the customer is refunded the prepaid fees for the unexpired part of the term, pro rata.

DRAFTING NOTES (integration)

- Insert as clause 7 of the agreement; the defined terms 'Supplier', 'Customer' and any cross-referenced notices clause are taken from the body of the agreement. If the agreement has no notices clause, clause 7.2 operates on actual receipt at the addressee's registered office or last notified address.
- Calculation illustration for consistency: on a 365-day Term with Fees of £36,500 (£100 per day), a notice received on day 100 takes effect on day 100, the agreement terminates on day 130 (Termination Date), the unexpired part is 235 whole days, and the refund is 36,500 x 235/365 = £23,500, payable within 30 days after day 130 (i.e. by day 160). Refund amount is always between £0 and the Fees paid.
- If the Customer is a consumer rather than a business, the clause should be reviewed for fairness under the Consumer Rights Act 2015 and the Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 before use; the drafting above is intended for a business-to-business subscription.
